name: Afternoon Tea at The Ritz
title: 12 Best Afternoon Teas in London 2026
description: The most iconic afternoon tea in London — possibly the world. Palm Court's gilded mirrors and ornate ceiling make this pure theatre. Strict dress code (jacket and tie for men) adds to the occasion. Book weeks ahead, especially for weekends.
highlights: First-time afternoon tea experience in Mayfair

name: Afternoon Tea at Claridge's
title: 12 Best Afternoon Teas in London 2026
description: If The Ritz is pomp, Claridge's is poise. The food is outstanding and the service impeccable. Hard to book at peak times but worth the effort. The Art Deco foyer is stunning and the pastry work is among London's best.
highlights: Refined luxury without theatrics in Mayfair

name: The Promenade at The Dorchester
title: 12 Best Afternoon Teas in London 2026
description: Right on Park Lane with Corinthian columns and plush chairs, The Dorchester's Promenade is a grand setting for tea. Reddit reviewers ranked it best for sandwiches, and the tea room itself is spacious and elegant — a cut above many competitors.
highlights: Grand hotel tea with the best sandwiches

name: The Drawing Room at Brown's Hotel
title: 12 Best Afternoon Teas in London 2026
description: The highest-rated afternoon tea on Google (4.8★) for good reason. Queen Victoria reportedly took tea here. The Drawing Room has wood paneling, live piano music, and a cosy atmosphere. Also offers a Tea-Tox healthy option. Reddit's pick for best overall experience.
highlights: Cosy, quintessentially English experience

name: sketch
title: 12 Best Afternoon Teas in London 2026
description: London's most photographed afternoon tea. The pink Gallery room is wildly photogenic, with egg-shaped pod toilets that are a destination in themselves. Whimsical patisserie and well-made scones. More about the experience than pure food quality, but the pastries are genuinely clever.
highlights: Friends who want a fun, Instagram-worthy afternoon

name: The Diamond Jubilee Tea Salon at Fortnum & Mason
title: 12 Best Afternoon Teas in London 2026
description: The Diamond Jubilee Tea Salon was opened by Queen Elizabeth II herself. You can choose between the traditional and savoury tea menus, and refills are included — so one person can get each and share. The tea selection is outstanding, sourced from their legendary 300-year-old shop downstairs.
highlights: Tea connoisseurs and quintessential British heritage

name: Afternoon Tea at Corinthia London
title: 12 Best Afternoon Teas in London 2026
description: Served under a spectacular glass-domed atrium with a massive Baccarat crystal chandelier. The pastries here are miniature works of art — more like jewels than food. The most photogenic afternoon tea for food photography. Note: seating is open-plan by the lobby, which some find less intimate.
highlights: Pastry lovers and special birthdays

name: The Rosebery at Mandarin Oriental Hyde Park
title: 12 Best Afternoon Teas in London 2026
description: A bloggers' favourite that flies slightly under the radar compared to The Ritz and Claridge's. The Rosebery has lots of natural light streaming through picture windows, comfy spring-green sofas, and a leisurely, unrushed pace. Hyde Park is right around the corner for a post-tea stroll.
highlights: A relaxed, unrushed afternoon with Hyde Park nearby

name: Afternoon Tea at The Savoy
title: 12 Best Afternoon Teas in London 2026
description: The Savoy's Thames Foyer has a live pianist and unlimited sandwiches — if you're hungry, it's one of the best deals at this price point. The cakes are creative, and they offer lower-sugar alternatives like chia puddings and chocolate strawberries. The space is immensely comfortable and gorgeous.
highlights: Hungry tea-goers who want unlimited sandwiches

name: The Goring
title: 12 Best Afternoon Teas in London 2026
description: The most royally connected afternoon tea in London. The Queen Mum was a regular, and Kate Middleton stayed the night before the Royal Wedding. A privately owned heritage hotel near Buckingham Palace that offers traditional British afternoon tea with impeccable service. Choose between The Dining Room or The Veranda.
highlights: Royal heritage and proximity to Buckingham Palace

name: Rosewood London
title: 12 Best Afternoon Teas in London 2026
description: Reddit's hidden gem pick. Still fairly under the radar, making it easier to book than The Ritz or Claridge's. The food is always amazing and they normally theme their designs around an artist. A local favourite that consistently impresses first-time guests. Best display presentation of any London afternoon tea.
highlights: Easier bookings and artistic presentation

name: The Lanesborough
title: 12 Best Afternoon Teas in London 2026
description: Fine detail in pastry work and an elegant pace to service. The Lanesborough runs themed teas that change regularly, so check what's on before you book. Scones arrive steaming with fragrant jams. Particularly good for dietary accommodations — gluten-free options are well above average.
highlights: Themed teas and excellent gluten-free options

description: Dishoom is the runaway winner of every London brunch poll on Reddit — and for good reason.

highlights: Matcha lovers and anyone wanting a peaceful escape from tourist crowds

name: Les 5 Marches

highlights: Brunch near Rue de l'Abreuvoir with excellent coffee and food

name: Devotions Café
title: 12 Best Cafés in Montmartre
description: Where specialty coffee meets creative mixology — try a beetroot latte and expand your horizons.
highlights: Adventurous drinkers who want more than a standard espresso

name: Dose Café

description: Two locations, one mission: perfectly brewed artisan coffee steps from Montmartre's iconic staircases.
highlights: A quick, high-quality coffee near Lamarck-Caulaincourt metro

name: Café Francoeur
title: 12 Best Cafés in Montmartre
description: The quintessential Montmartre café — morning espresso to late-night wine, with 2,000+ reviews to prove it.
highlights: The classic Parisian café experience from dawn to late night

name: Bob's Bake Shop
title: 12 Best Cafés in Montmartre
description: A slice of Brooklyn in the 18th — NYC-style bagels and honest filter coffee in a laid-back setting.
highlights: NYC-quality bagels with good filter coffee for a casual morning

name: St-Viateur Bagel
title: 10 Best Montreal's Wood-Fired Bagels (2026)
description: The most famous bagel shop in Montreal, and one of the most iconic in the world. St-Viateur uses a wood-burning oven and has been making hand-rolled, honey-water-boiled bagels since 1957. The sesame bagel here is the benchmark against which all others are judged.
highlights: The definitive Montreal bagel experience — iconic location, wood-fired oven, 24 hours

name: Fairmount Bagel
title: 10 Best Montreal's Wood-Fired Bagels (2026)
description: The oldest bagel shop in North America, open since 1919. Fairmount's bagels are slightly different from St-Viateur — a bit denser and sweeter. The eternal debate between these two shops is one of Montreal's great food controversies.
highlights: The oldest bagel bakery in North America, slightly sweeter and denser than St-Viateur

name: Bagel St-Lo
title: 10 Best Montreal's Wood-Fired Bagels (2026)
description: A newer entrant that has rapidly built a following in Rosemont. Bagel St-Lo uses traditional wood-fired technique but adds some creative varieties. Many locals say these are the best everyday bagels in the city — consistently excellent and slightly underrated.
highlights: Best newcomer bagel in Montreal, Rosemont neighbourhood, creative varieties

name: R.E.A.L. Bagel
title: 10 Best Montreal's Wood-Fired Bagels (2026)
description: A respected bagel institution that flies under the tourist radar. R.E.A.L. Bagel uses traditional methods and produces consistently excellent bagels. A great option for exploring bagels beyond the St-Viateur/Fairmount rivalry.
locationLabel: Off the main tourist strip, Montreal
highlights: Traditional bagels off the tourist trail

name: Bagel Etc
title: 10 Best Montreal's Wood-Fired Bagels (2026)
description: More than just a bagel shop — Bagel Etc is a beloved brunch institution on The Main. Famous for huge bagel sandwiches loaded with smoked salmon, cream cheese, and toppings. The weekend brunch queue is worth it.
highlights: Bagel sandwiches and brunch, The Main location, casual neighbourhood dining

name: Premier Bagel
title: 10 Best Montreal's Wood-Fired Bagels (2026)
description: The 'secret third option' in the Fairmount vs St-Viateur debate, according to Reddit. Premier Bagel in CDN serves wood-fired Montreal bagels that many locals prefer. Less touristy, equally excellent, and a great choice if you're in Côte-des-Neiges.
highlights: The secret third bagel option — less touristy, equally excellent

name: Le Trou
title: 10 Best Montreal's Wood-Fired Bagels (2026)
description: An artisan bagel shop in Mile End that combines traditional Montreal technique with modern sensibility. Le Trou makes bagels that respect heritage while being slightly more creative with flavours and fillings. A good option for bagel lovers who want something slightly different.
highlights: Artisan Montreal bagels with modern twist, Mile End exploration

name: Beauty's Luncheonette (bagels)
title: 10 Best Montreal's Wood-Fired Bagels (2026)
description: While primarily famous for brunch, Beauty's serves excellent bagel-based dishes including the iconic Mish-Mash omelette and bagel with lox. A great place to experience Montreal bagels in a classic deli context rather than straight from a bakery.
highlights: Bagels in a classic deli context, iconic Montreal brunch institution

name: Monsieur B
title: 10 Best Montreal's Wood-Fired Bagels (2026)
description: A modern Plateau brunch spot that does creative things with Montreal bagels. Monsieur B uses locally sourced ingredients and house-baked goods to create elevated bagel sandwiches and brunch dishes. Perfect for those who want their bagel tradition with a contemporary twist.
highlights: Modern bagel-based brunch, creative toppings, Plateau neighbourhood dining

name: Yiddish World
title: 10 Best Montreal's Wood-Fired Bagels (2026)
description: A cultural experience as much as a food experience — Yiddish World celebrates Montreal's Jewish deli tradition through bagels and traditional Eastern European foods. The bagels here are excellent and the cultural context adds meaning to every bite.
locationLabel: Near the old Jewish Quarter, Plateau
highlights: Bagels in cultural/historical Jewish deli context, Plateau neighbourhood

name: Olive et Gourmando
title: 10 Best Best Brunch Spots in Montreal (2026)
description: The most beloved brunch spot in Old Montreal — famous for pastries, sandwiches, and breakfast bowls that are worth the wait. Olive et Gourmando's warm, artisan-bakery atmosphere and consistently excellent food have made it a pilgrimage for food lovers visiting Montreal.
highlights: Best brunch in Old Montreal — pastries, sandwiches, warm ambiance

name: Arthur's Nosh Bar
title: 10 Best Best Brunch Spots in Montreal (2026)
description: A vibrant brunch spot in Saint-Henri known for its New York deli-inspired menu with a Montreal twist. Arthur's serves excellent smoked fish, bagels, and creative brunch dishes in a lively atmosphere. One of the city's most talked-about newer brunch destinations.
highlights: New York deli-inspired brunch, Saint-Henri neighbourhood dining

name: Foiegwa
title: 10 Best Best Brunch Spots in Montreal (2026)
description: An elevated brunch experience downtown that pushes boundaries with creative Québecois-influenced dishes. Foiegwa brings French technique and seasonal Quebec ingredients to weekend brunch, resulting in dishes that feel special without being stuffy.
highlights: Elevated brunch downtown, creative Quebec-inspired dishes, special occasions

name: Junior
title: 10 Best Best Brunch Spots in Montreal (2026)
description: A cozy Mile End brunch spot that has become a neighbourhood institution faster than most expected. Junior serves creative, well-executed brunch dishes in a warm, unpretentious atmosphere. The weekend queue tells you everything you need to know.
highlights: Mile End neighbourhood brunch, cozy atmosphere, creative dishes

name: Bar George
title: 10 Best Best Brunch Spots in Montreal (2026)
description: The upscale brunch at Hotel William Gray's restaurant — a beautiful space with excellent service and a menu that excels at refined versions of brunch classics. Best for a special occasion or when you want to impress visiting friends with Old Montreal's grandeur.
locationLabel: Hotel William Gray, 421 St-Vincent, Old Montreal
highlights: Special occasion brunch, upscale Old Montreal setting, hotel dining

name: Le Café Bloom
title: 10 Best Best Brunch Spots in Montreal (2026)
description: A charming neighbourhood brunch café in Westmount with excellent pastries, good coffee, and a warm, floral atmosphere. Le Café Bloom has become a go-to for Westmount locals and is worth the visit if you're in that area.
highlights: Westmount neighbourhood brunch café, great pastries, warm atmosphere

name: MARCUS Restaurant + Lounge
title: 10 Best Best Brunch Spots in Montreal (2026)
description: Celebrity chef Marcus Samuelsson's Montreal outpost serves a brunch that reflects his global perspective — Ethiopian-influenced dishes alongside classic Quebec ingredients. A unique brunch experience that goes beyond what most Montreal spots offer.
highlights: Celebrity chef brunch, global cuisine, special occasion, downtown location

name: Beauty's Luncheonette
title: 10 Best Best Brunch Spots in Montreal (2026)
description: Montreal's most iconic brunch diner, open since 1942. The Mish-Mash omelette (salami, green pepper, onion, beef salami) is legendary and worth the weekend queue. Beauty's is a cultural institution as much as a restaurant.
highlights: Iconic Montreal brunch diner, legendary Mish-Mash omelette, cultural institution

name: La Binerie Mont-Royal
title: 10 Best Best Brunch Spots in Montreal (2026)
description: A genuine Quebec comfort food institution famous for fèves au lard (baked beans) and old-school Québecois breakfast. La Binerie was featured in Michel Tremblay's novels and remains a cultural touchstone for Montreal's working-class food heritage.
highlights: Authentic old-school Québecois breakfast, cultural heritage, budget dining

name: Café Pista
title: 10 Best Best Brunch Spots in Montreal (2026)
description: One of the best newer brunch spots on the Plateau, Café Pista brings creative, globally-influenced dishes to the neighbourhood. Known for excellent coffee and brunch dishes that feel thought-through rather than assembled. The weekend queue is well-managed.
highlights: Modern creative brunch on the Plateau, excellent coffee, creative dishes

name: Broue Pub Brouhaha
title: 10 Best Montreal's Craft Beer Scene (2026)
description: Montreal's beloved neighbourhood brewpub with multiple locations — known for a rotating selection of house-brewed ales, excellent food, and an unpretentious atmosphere that feels genuinely local. Brouhaha is where Reddit consistently sends people for the best overall craft beer experience in Montreal.
highlights: Best overall brewpub experience, multiple neighbourhood locations, house-brewed ales

name: Mellön Brasserie
title: 10 Best Montreal's Craft Beer Scene (2026)
description: One of Montreal's most acclaimed newer microbreweries, Mellön consistently produces creative and well-crafted beers across styles. Their taproom on The Main is an excellent spot to sample the range, and the food pairs excellently with the beers.
highlights: Best newer microbrewery, creative beer styles, The Main taproom

name: Brasserie Harricana
title: 10 Best Montreal's Craft Beer Scene (2026)
description: Set in a beautiful old building in Mile End/Outremont, Brasserie Harricana has quickly established itself as one of Montreal's best brewery experiences — both for the beer quality and the stunning space. Their seasonal and limited releases are particularly sought after.
highlights: Best brewery space in Montreal, limited releases, Mile End neighbourhood

name: Isle de Garde
title: 10 Best Montreal's Craft Beer Scene (2026)
description: A beloved Plateau brewpub that specializes in Belgian and farmhouse-style ales. Isle de Garde has a warm, inviting atmosphere and produces some of the most distinctive beers in the city — particularly their saisons and bières de garde (as the name suggests).
highlights: Belgian-style ales, farmhouse beers, Plateau neighbourhood, cozy atmosphere

name: Les Sans-Taverne
title: 10 Best Montreal's Craft Beer Scene (2026)
description: A microbrewery with multiple taproom locations across Montreal, Les Sans-Taverne has built a loyal following for consistent quality across a wide range of styles. Their IPAs and lagers are particularly well-regarded.
highlights: Consistent craft beer across styles, multiple locations, reliable quality

name: Mabrasserie
title: 10 Best Montreal's Craft Beer Scene (2026)
description: A neighbourhood gem in Hochelaga-Maisonneuve that's part of the neighbourhood's revival. Mabrasserie makes excellent community-focused beers and has become a social hub in an increasingly vibrant part of Montreal. Great for exploring beyond the tourist areas.
highlights: Off-tourist-trail brewery, HoMa neighbourhood, community atmosphere

name: Boswell Brasserie Artisanale
title: 10 Best Montreal's Craft Beer Scene (2026)
description: A neighbourhood brewpub on the Plateau East offering friendly service, craft beers brewed on site, and excellent food at good prices. Boswell is the kind of local brewpub that every neighbourhood should have — unpretentious, excellent, and deeply connected to its community.
highlights: Neighbourhood brewpub experience, Plateau East, friendly service

name: Brasserie Silo
title: 10 Best Montreal's Craft Beer Scene (2026)
description: A well-regarded microbrewery in Saint-Henri that's part of that neighbourhood's creative renaissance. Brasserie Silo makes bold, distinctive beers in a beautiful converted industrial space — one of the best brewery atmospheres in the city.
highlights: Industrial brewery atmosphere, Saint-Henri neighbourhood, bold beers

name: Etoh Brasserie
title: 10 Best Montreal's Craft Beer Scene (2026)
description: An East Montreal microbrewery that specializes in experimental and small-batch beers. Etoh has built a following among serious craft beer enthusiasts for pushing boundaries and never playing it safe with their brewing.
highlights: Experimental small-batch beers, East Montreal, serious craft beer enthusiasts

name: Le Cheval Blanc
title: 10 Best Montreal's Craft Beer Scene (2026)
description: One of the original craft beer bars in Quebec — Le Cheval Blanc opened in 1985 and has been a pioneer of the Quebec craft beer movement. A historic spot with reliable quality and deep cultural significance for anyone interested in the history of craft beer in Canada.
highlights: Original Quebec craft beer bar, beer history, affordable pints, classic atmosphere

name: La Banquise
title: 12 Best Poutine Spots in Montreal (2026)
description: Montreal's most famous poutine restaurant, open 24/7 with over 70 poutine varieties. From the classic La Banquise to loaded versions with smoked meat or pulled pork, this Plateau institution has been feeding Montrealers and tourists since 1968. The best post-bar poutine run in the city.
highlights: The quintessential Montreal poutine experience — huge menu, iconic location, 24h access

name: Casse-Normand
title: 12 Best Poutine Spots in Montreal (2026)
description: Reddit's consensus choice for the best pure poutine in Montreal. Casse-Normand in Verdun doesn't try to be fancy — just perfect fries (crunchy outside, soft inside), amazing gravy, and fresh curds. The kind of place locals are almost reluctant to share.
highlights: The best classic poutine execution in Montreal by local consensus

name: Poutineville
title: 12 Best Poutine Spots in Montreal (2026)
description: The "build-your-own-poutine" concept that became a Montreal staple. Choose your fry type, gravy, toppings — from pulled pork to truffle oil to lobster. Fun for groups and adventurous eaters who want to go beyond the classic three-ingredient version.
highlights: Creative poutine, groups, and anyone who wants wild topping combinations

name: Montreal Pool Room
title: 12 Best Poutine Spots in Montreal (2026)
description: A Montreal institution since 1912. The steamé hot dogs and poutine here have fed generations of late-night revellers stumbling off The Main. It's not the fanciest poutine in the city, but there's something irreplaceable about eating at this counter at 2am.
highlights: Late-night poutine, budget eating, old-school Montreal atmosphere

name: Chez Claudette
title: 12 Best Poutine Spots in Montreal (2026)
description: A neighbourhood institution in the Plateau that predates the poutine tourism wave. Chez Claudette serves honest, excellent poutine with generous curds and rich gravy in a welcoming diner atmosphere. One of the best "community hub" poutine spots in the city.
highlights: Classic neighbourhood diner poutine with authentic Plateau atmosphere

name: Patati Patata
title: 12 Best Poutine Spots in Montreal (2026)
description: Tiny counter-seating diner on The Main with huge soul. Patati Patata has been serving excellent, affordable poutine (and legendary burgers) for decades. The space fits maybe 15 people, which makes it feel like a secret even though it's beloved across the city.
highlights: Budget poutine on The Main, counter dining atmosphere, burgers + poutine combo

name: Chez Tousignant
title: 12 Best Poutine Spots in Montreal (2026)
description: A newer entry that quickly became a neighbourhood staple in Rosemont-La Petite-Patrie. Chez Tousignant uses quality ingredients and traditional techniques, resulting in poutine that rivals the old-school institutions. A great option if you're exploring the Beaubien Street area.
highlights: Quality poutine in Rosemont, great neighbourhood atmosphere

name: Greenspot
title: 12 Best Poutine Spots in Montreal (2026)
description: One of Montreal's oldest remaining diners, open since 1941 in Saint-Henri. Greenspot serves classic Quebec diner food including excellent poutine in a time-capsule atmosphere. The kind of place where locals have been eating the same booth for 30 years.
highlights: Old-school Montreal diner atmosphere, classic Quebec comfort food

name: Ma Poule Mouillée
title: 12 Best Poutine Spots in Montreal (2026)
description: Right next to La Banquise, Ma Poule Mouillée is famous for its chicken (poule) but the poutine is equally stellar. A Plateau institution that locals often prefer over its more famous neighbour for shorter waits and equally good quality.
locationLabel: 969 Rachel St E, Plateau (near La Banquise)
highlights: Poutine + excellent rotisserie chicken combo, Plateau location, shorter wait than La Banquise

name: Chez Ma Tante
title: 12 Best Poutine Spots in Montreal (2026)
description: A cozy Outremont diner serving traditional Québecois food including excellent poutine. "Chez Ma Tante" (Aunt's house) captures the warmth and comfort of home cooking. A great option for anyone exploring the Outremont or Mile-End area.
highlights: Cozy Québecois diner atmosphere, Outremont / Mile-End area exploration

name: Méchant Boeuf Bar Brasserie
title: 12 Best Poutine Spots in Montreal (2026)
description: The upscale Old Montreal brasserie that proves poutine can be fine dining. Their braised beef poutine with rich house-made gravy is one of the best elevated poutine experiences in the city. Perfect if you're in Old Montreal and want poutine without sacrificing atmosphere.
highlights: Gourmet poutine in Old Montreal, date night, impressive out-of-town guests

name: Mont-Royal Hot-Dog
title: 12 Best Poutine Spots in Montreal (2026)
description: A no-frills Plateau diner serving solid poutine alongside their famous hot dogs. Mont-Royal Hot-Dog is the kind of place that's been feeding the neighbourhood for decades without changing a thing — and that's exactly why locals love it.
highlights: Classic diner poutine, budget eats, Plateau neighbourhood atmosphere

name: Schwartz's Deli
title: 10 Best Montreal Smoked Meat Delis (2026)
description: The most famous smoked meat deli in the world. Schwartz's has been serving medium-fat smoked meat sandwiches since 1928 and the queue down St-Laurent is part of the Montreal experience.
highlights: The iconic Montreal smoked meat experience — the original and most famous

name: Snowdon Deli
title: 10 Best Montreal Smoked Meat Delis (2026)
description: Many locals argue Snowdon Deli serves the best smoked meat in Montreal — better than Schwartz's, with friendlier service and shorter waits. A family institution with decades of loyal regulars.
highlights: Best bang-for-your-buck smoked meat, local favourite over tourists

name: Smoke Meat Pete
title: 10 Best Montreal Smoked Meat Delis (2026)
description: Technically just outside Montreal on Île-Perrot, but Reddit consistently ranks this as one of the best — if not the best — smoked meat in the Greater Montreal area. Worth the drive, especially in summer when they have outdoor seating.
highlights: Best smoked meat if you have a car, worth the trip from Montreal

name: Lester's Deli
title: 10 Best Montreal Smoked Meat Delis (2026)
description: A beloved Outremont institution serving excellent smoked meat in a warm, family-run deli atmosphere. Lester's has been a neighbourhood anchor for generations and offers a slightly less touristy experience than Schwartz's.
highlights: Classic smoked meat in a warm family deli atmosphere, Outremont area

name: Dunn's Famous
title: 10 Best Montreal Smoked Meat Delis (2026)
description: The most centrally located and accessible smoked meat option downtown, open very late. Dunn's is a chain so quality purists prefer the independents, but for tourists who want smoked meat near their hotel after midnight, it's a solid option.
highlights: Late night smoked meat downtown, tourist-friendly location

name: Beauty's Luncheonette
title: 10 Best Montreal Smoked Meat Delis (2026)
description: An iconic Plateau institution since 1942 famous for the 'Mish-Mash' omelette and classic deli food. Not exclusively smoked meat but their version is excellent — and the brunch queue is almost as famous as Schwartz's lunch lineup.
highlights: Classic Montreal deli atmosphere with smoked meat + famous brunch

name: Reuben's Deli
title: 10 Best Montreal Smoked Meat Delis (2026)
description: A downtown Montreal deli staple that has fed shoppers and workers on Ste-Catherine for decades. Reuben's serves a solid smoked meat sandwich in a classic deli setting, making it the easiest option if you're shopping downtown and need a proper meal.
highlights: Downtown smoked meat while shopping or sightseeing on Ste-Catherine

name: Mile End Deli
title: 10 Best Montreal Smoked Meat Delis (2026)
description: A modern take on the classic Montreal deli in the Mile End neighbourhood. Mile End Deli uses house-cured meats and locally sourced ingredients, resulting in smoked meat that satisfies both traditionalists and food-forward diners.
highlights: Artisan take on smoked meat, Mile End neighbourhood dining

name: Katz's Delicatessen (Montreal)
title: 10 Best Montreal Smoked Meat Delis (2026)

name: Mercado 20 de Noviembre
title: 12 Best Street Food in Oaxaca (2026)
description: The beating heart of Oaxacan food culture. The Pasillo de Humo (Smoke Alley) is a sensory overload — vendors grilling tasajo, chorizo, and cecina over open charcoal. You pick your protein, they grill it, and a neighboring stall provides tortillas, salsa, and sides.
highlights: First-time visitors — the ultimate Oaxacan food immersion

name: Tlayudas La Chinita
title: 12 Best Street Food in Oaxaca (2026)
description: The most famous tlayuda stall in Oaxaca, featured on Netflix's Street Food. A late-night institution where a team chars chorizo, coaxes tasajo to perfection, and flips massive moon-shaped tortillas over charcoal.
locationLabel: C. de Nuño del Mercado 209, Centro
highlights: Late-night tlayudas after a mezcal crawl

name: Tacos del Carmen
title: 12 Best Street Food in Oaxaca (2026)
description: Operating since 1977. Chef Alejandro Ruiz endorses the tacos de chile relleno — stuffed peppers rolled in tortillas that are spicy, meaty, and tender. A block from Santo Domingo Church.
highlights: Afternoon taco fix near Santo Domingo

name: Empanadas del Carmen
title: 12 Best Street Food in Oaxaca (2026)
description: Evening counterpart to Tacos del Carmen next door. Specializes in empanadas de amarillo — large corn tortillas folded around yellow mole, shredded chicken, and hoja santa. Chef Ruiz: 'cheap and delicious.'
highlights: Evening snack — perfect pre-mezcal fuel

name: Memelas Doña Vale
title: 12 Best Street Food in Oaxaca (2026)
description: Doña Vale has been grilling memelas for 40 years. Chef Ruiz's #1 pick: 'Five options, no more. I love these kinds of places.'
highlights: Breakfast memelas in a working-class market

name: Las Tlayudas de Mina y Bustamante
title: 12 Best Street Food in Oaxaca (2026)
description: Where locals send you for the best tlayudas. Off the beaten trail beyond the Zócalo, you'll smell the charcoal before you see it. Portions are enormous.
locationLabel: C. de Carlos María Bustamante 322, Centro
highlights: Late-night tlayudas with fewer tourists

name: Memelas San Agustín
title: 12 Best Street Food in Oaxaca (2026)
description: A roadside stall with incredible variety — chicken tinga, chicharrón, pico de gallo, salpicón. The señoras clearly have a passion for what they do.
locationLabel: C. de Manuel Fernández Fiallo 309, Centro
highlights: Breakfast or lunch memelas with creative toppings

name: Tortas La Hormiga
title: 12 Best Street Food in Oaxaca (2026)
description: A Oaxacan institution in picturesque Jardín Conzatti park. The line is always long but moves fast. Tortas are grilled panini-style on puffy white bread with quesillo, pickled veggies, and your choice of filling.
locationLabel: Valentín Gómez Farias S/N, Centro (Jardín Conzatti)
highlights: Lunch in the park — Oaxaca's best tortas

name: Mercado Benito Juárez
title: 12 Best Street Food in Oaxaca (2026)
description: The other essential Oaxacan market, right next to Mercado 20 de Noviembre. More focused on shopping (chapulines, chocolate, mole paste, quesillo, mezcal) but with excellent food stalls too. The cheese vendors alone are worth the trip.
highlights: Stocking up on Oaxacan ingredients + quick market bites

name: Fonda Rosita
title: 12 Best Street Food in Oaxaca (2026)

name: The Salmon
title: 12 Best Seafood Restaurants in Oslo
description: Oslo's highest-rated seafood restaurant is dedicated entirely to Norwegian salmon — grilled, smoked, cured, and raw. The waterfront location at Aker Brygge with fjord views makes it a destination in itself.

name: Vulkanfisk
title: 12 Best Seafood Restaurants in Oslo
description: The best-value seafood in Oslo, located inside the Mathallen food hall in the Grünerløkka neighborhood. Counter-service format with outstanding fish soup, fish and chips, and daily specials using whatever came off the boats that morning.

name: Lofotstua
title: 12 Best Seafood Restaurants in Oslo
description: The definitive traditional Norwegian fish restaurant in Oslo. Located in the Majorstuen neighborhood away from the tourist waterfront, this is where locals go for authentic Norwegian seafood — stockfish, klippfisk, bacalao, and seasonal catches prepared the way Norwegians have eaten them for centuries.

name: Solsiden Restaurant
title: 12 Best Seafood Restaurants in Oslo
description: The fine-dining seafood option with an unbeatable waterfront location along Akershusstranda. Solsiden focuses on seasonal Norwegian seafood prepared with contemporary Nordic technique. Pricey but worth it for a special occasion.

name: Fiskeriet Youngstorget
title: 12 Best Seafood Restaurants in Oslo
description: Part fishmonger, part restaurant — Fiskeriet operates as a fish counter where you can buy fresh seafood to take home or sit down for a casual meal. The Youngstorget location is the original and most popular. Quality is high and prices are fair by Oslo standards.

name: Louise Restaurant & Bar
title: 12 Best Seafood Restaurants in Oslo
description: The most popular restaurant on the Aker Brygge waterfront by review count. Louise serves a broad seafood-focused menu in a buzzy brasserie atmosphere. The fish soup alone is worth a visit. Good for groups and couples who want waterfront dining without the formality of fine dining.

name: Lofoten Fiskerestaurant
title: 12 Best Seafood Restaurants in Oslo
description: One of Oslo's most established upscale seafood restaurants, with a prime location on the Aker Brygge waterfront looking out over the Oslofjord. Named after the Lofoten Islands — Norway's premier fishing region — the restaurant takes its sourcing seriously.

name: Rorbua Aker Brygge
title: 12 Best Seafood Restaurants in Oslo
description: A rorbua is a traditional Norwegian fisherman's cabin — and this Aker Brygge restaurant recreates that rustic seaside atmosphere. The menu focuses on hearty, traditional Norwegian seafood at prices that are more accessible than its upscale neighbors on the same waterfront strip.

name: Sjømagasinet
title: 12 Best Seafood Restaurants in Oslo
description: Located on the fashionable Tjuvholmen peninsula — Oslo's newest waterfront development — Sjømagasinet is a refined fine-dining seafood restaurant. The setting is modern and elegant, and the kitchen treats Norwegian seafood with Nordic fine-dining technique.

name: Skur 33
title: 12 Best Seafood Restaurants in Oslo
description: Named after the harbor warehouse it occupies, Skur 33 sits right on the waterfront near the Akershus Fortress. The atmosphere is industrial-chic with exposed beams and harbor views. A reliable mid-range seafood option that Redditors recommend as an alternative to the more tourist-heavy Aker Brygge strip.

name: Restaurant Havsmak
title: 12 Best Seafood Restaurants in Oslo
description: Located near the Oslo Opera House, Havsmak ("taste of the ocean") is a fine-dining seafood restaurant that focuses on sustainably sourced Norwegian seafood. The lower review count reflects its more exclusive, reservation-only nature rather than any quality concern — Redditors mention it in the same breath as Lofoten for price and quality.

name: Fiskeriet Bjørvika
title: 12 Best Seafood Restaurants in Oslo
description: The newer, second location of Fiskeriet — situated in the modern Bjørvika waterfront district near the Oslo Opera House and Munch Museum. Same quality fishmonger-restaurant concept as Youngstorget, with a slightly more modern setting and proximity to Oslo's cultural attractions.
